mechanics.name: Salvation's Cry
mechanics.currentEffect: Whenever the Killer starts chasing you, you see the Auras of all other Survivors for 1/2/3 seconds. Every Survivor who is not being chased sees your Aura and the Killer's Aura for 5 seconds.
activation: The Killer must start chasing you.
Ends/deactivates when: Aura reveals end after their stated durations.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (10.1.0): Added as a new Aurora Stardotter perk; no later live balance change verified.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: When a chase starts on you, briefly shares Survivor and Killer locations with everyone not in chase.
duration: Other Survivors' Auras are visible to you for 1/2/3 seconds.
Your Aura and the Killer's Aura are visible to each Survivor not being chased for 5 seconds.
specialInteractions: The shared Aura reveal is limited to Survivors who are not currently being chased.

editorial.summary: When the Killer starts chasing you, briefly show teammates to you and show both you and the Killer to every teammate not in chase.
useCases: Give the entire team immediate Killer information when your chase begins.
Help teammates know whether the chase is moving toward their generator or rescue path.
Use the brief teammate Auras to route away from active objectives.
counters: Only triggers when a chase officially begins.
The user sees teammates for only up to 3 seconds.
Teammates already in chase do not receive the same team-information package.
pros: Teamwide information from a natural chase event.
No cooldown or setup stated in the current effect.
Particularly useful for SWF-like coordination in Solo Q.
cons: Official chase detection can occasionally behave differently from player intuition.
analysis: Salvation's Cry lands at this position because it broadcasts one of the most important match facts, the start of a chase, to the rest of the team. Survivors not being chased see both the chased Survivor and the Killer for five seconds.

That information immediately answers macro questions. A teammate can stay on a generator if the Killer is moving away, rotate early if the chase is coming toward them, or abandon a risky rescue path before the Killer arrives.

The chased player also gets a short teammate Aura snapshot, helping them avoid dragging the Killer onto active objectives. That overlaps conceptually with Quick Gambit, though without the repair-speed bonus.
It remains B because the perk changes information rather than chase physics. The team must convert the five-second read into better decisions for the slot to matter.
editorial.verdict: A clean team-information perk that makes chase starts visible to everyone. Salvation's Cry is especially valuable when Solo Q needs SWF-like awareness without voice comms.
